name: Transaction value

subjectOf.text: No consensus protocol can guard against Byzantine faults when a single transaction is worth more than the promise of all future fees for the entire platform, because in that case a party can profitably bribe the whole node set to destroy the chain's own integrity.
subjectOf.abstract: No protocol can guard against Byzantine faults if a transaction is more valuable than the promise of all future fees for the entire platform; in this case a party could bribe the entire set of nodes (or 51%)
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Secure Proof of Stake Protocol (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3125827
scope_conditions: a single transaction whose value exceeds the present value of all future platform fees

subjectOf.text: Altruism cannot be relied on in a decentralized anonymous system, so fees are ultimately crucial; the authors conclude that several blockchains with different fee structures must exist so that different transaction values can be given correspondingly different security.
